review_instruction: Finding a real issue is a successful review.

findings: The town separates into an upper cluster and a sparse lower row instead of reading as one interlocked mass.
Large temporary bearing columns dominate the silhouette.
Ground-route slabs remain exposed to open grass on long edges.
Upper circulation is continuous but resembles one fenced rooftop deck rather than a path threaded between facades.
Several lower buildings read as visual islands despite graph-connected addresses.
The sectional silhouette exposes tall empty support shafts instead of inhabited or terrain-borne lower mass.
The city can still be read through vertically in the core.
The entrance is not visually framed as the mouth of a winding alley.
The review camera also needs a route-tangent-derived target that proves the named circulation segment.
A broad fenced platform dominates the view; adjacent building entrances and the continuing route are not legible.
The camera does not isolate the occupied skywalk well enough to prove both facade joins.
The occupied overhead volume and external stairs create the intended buried-in-city effect locally.
The surrounding route still opens directly to grass and does not sustain that effect beyond the motif.
Roof closure is substantially improved, but the plan remains visibly split into disconnected-looking islands and exposed route slabs.
